batch_strategy: Select 32 experiments that resolve structure-specific solvent response, test loading interactions where predictions are nearly invariant, and extend coverage through chemically interpretable analogues. Use recent acquisition errors to revise hypotheses, with the observed table governing molecule and condition identities. Treat quantile widths as secondary model-behavior evidence.

choices.reason: m211 at 10/1, 100 ul begins a fixed-loading 10/1-to-20/1 pair between measured 5/1 1ce749f818905d3c61d4 and 50/1 449b809e4efaaf2af86a. It tests where the phenylpyridine response accelerates, beyond its relatively compact measured 5/1 behavior.

m211 at 20/1 completes that solvent bracket with unchanged loading and plug conditions. The predicted 47.27/84.11 mL endpoints imply substantial growth beyond 10/1; the pair can teach the transition shape rather than a molecule-wide nitrogen offset.

m146 at 2/1 fills the strong-solvent side of measured 5/1 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e and 10/1 9e3ce3497298084abd83. Together with the selected quinoline point, it tests whether methyl substitution changes the early part of the solvent-response curve.

m216 at 2/1 supplies the quinoline counterpart at the same nominal sample volume and PE loading plug. Its prediction is almost identical to m146, despite their measured 5/1 and 10/1 differences in 1ae3618ec277b0463686, e47aebe2660b9e1528de, and the m146 records.

m160 at 2/1, 150 ul extends the para-aminobenzonitrile curve below measured 5/1 fe66b2381d33aa2ea3a8. Its pairing with the meta isomer tests whether their large measured onset difference at 5/1 develops gradually or locally.

m161 at 2/1 matches the selected m160 sample volume, DCM solvent, and 400-ul plug. Measured 3774a4dac6dd0f01d48d showed earlier onset than m160 at 5/1 while both had long completion volumes; this point tests positional effects on each endpoint.

m72 at 10/1, 50 ul in DCM supplies the lower-loading member of a controlled pair. Measured 10f01f359bc6067d009f at 5/1 and 8e7636d7a60a6058305a at 20/1 motivate an intermediate label, while the latter also differs in loading solvent and plug volume.

m72 at 10/1, 150 ul changes loading amount from 51.1 to 153.3 mg while preserving DCM and the 200-ul plug. Both selected predictions are approximately 27.2/78.1 mL. Their labels can distinguish loading sensitivity from the confounded 20/1 contrast involving 334f7f55dcbf278e47ec.

m205 at 0/1, 150 ul directly extends measured 1/1 1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7 at the same loading conditions. That acquisition still underestimated both endpoints substantially; pure EA tests whether the fused phenethyl-alcohol difference persists at the strongest mobile-phase boundary.

m206 at 2/1 fills the gap between measured 1/1 53ceb391785085223695 and 5/1 614873124b33029a924c. It also adds a lower-loading contrast. Comparison with the m205 curve can teach how OH spacing and aromatic attachment affect solvent response, with loading and plug differences retained.

m200 at 2/1 tests the nitro-alcohol completion response after measured 1/1 records 5da8c25a3982216fb112 and 7dace1dbecce79e17117, and 0/1 88d94bacb5a3b54ac7d1. Its predicted completion is slightly below the measured 1/1 values; the lower sample loading must be interpreted jointly with ratio.

m207 at 10/1, 50 ul extends measured 1/1 d803316212dc6eb862e9 at fixed loading conditions. The predicted 35.09/62.04 mL endpoints test transfer from other benzyl alcohols, including measured m135 75232f4ee5de52a0499e, into a brominated aromatic environment.

m26 at 10/1, 100 ul extends its measured 1/1 record e1888b5ca18659a8d8eb and begins a matched 10/1-to-50/1 pair. Benzoylacetone provides a diketone comparison to the beta-ketoesters implicated by the recent m25 failure.

m26 at 50/1 completes the fixed-loading pair. The predicted 31.27/78.22 mL endpoints are plausible but unmeasured; comparison with m25 3fc05dc2025715e68174 and the selected m81 rows tests whether PE-rich growth depends on the carbonyl and ester environment.

m81 at 50/1, 50 ul starts a controlled 55.5-to-111 mg loading comparison. Measured 7d402b3fad455f06fe68 and 6b8ff4c027d9c4c2d75f showed distinct high-loading behavior at 10/1 and 20/1; this pair tests transfer into the weaker-mobile-phase regime.

m81 at 50/1, 100 ul doubles sample amount at fixed ratio and DCM plug. The model gives essentially the same endpoints as the selected 50-ul row, despite loading contrasts in fa5d86f56c1c38fa9416, 06c0c99f1cfb752ed34b, 904c7849feb1c686924a, and 5879dc8ccb560446d54c.

m107 at 2/1, 150 ul brackets measured 5/1 2cfa393cb79664e100ce at fixed loading. The predicted 15.87/47.92 mL endpoints test how the ether-rich beta-ketoester enters its long-completion regime and whether that response transfers to m13 and m20.

m13 at 5/1 starts a fixed 56.1-mg solvent-response pair with the selected 10/1 row. Measured 81507d463506a9e65e73 and 2dbfdf9c2d5defd09f7a cover stronger mobile phases at higher loading, leaving the predicted rise in this multifunctional keto-diester untested.

m13 at 10/1 completes the same-loading pair. Its prediction rises from approximately 17.07/49.68 to 29.98/82.38 mL between 5/1 and 10/1. Measuring both points can distinguish a steep ratio response from a structural offset in multiacceptor ester predictions.

m20 at 10/1, 150 ul extends measured 2/1 65e1a58ab8e4aa2f1eb6 with unchanged loading conditions. This simpler ether-acrylate tests whether the predicted delayed regime transfers across ether-containing esters without the additional carbonyl groups of m13 and m107.

m178 at 5/1 supplies an actual intermediate label before measured 10/1 634f21e11a8442494ce3. The observed table identifies recent 17ff70c0f8a083dcf5f0 as m126 at 10/1, so it does not establish an m178 5/1 outcome. This selection resolves that remaining completion-response gap.

m195 at 10/1, 100 ul starts a matched 10/1-to-20/1 pair after measured 2/1 1194ed3b17f8c39d6111. It tests where onset rises sharply before the unusual nearly coincident endpoints recorded at 20/1 in a917c928912c74862968.

m195 at 20/1, 100 ul completes that pair and changes loading relative to measured 150-ul a917c928912c74862968, whose V1 slightly exceeded V2. It tests whether a compact elution interval persists or whether the earlier record reflects loading-dependent behavior or recording variability.

m129 at 50/1 extends the now-measured 2/1, 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1 sequence represented by e05652bb38d9efd5b11e, cf8ab33c25ad391a584c, 4c46ceefd6147b1e0a7a, and f4331eb64b6774466836. One boundary label tests extrapolation after the intermediate overpredictions have been exposed.

Previously unobserved m179 at 20/1 supplies the seven-membered fused cyclic ketone in a comparison with selected m180. Their similar recorded amounts and identical loading solvent and plug volume make ring-context transfer interpretable despite high fingerprint similarity.

m180 at 20/1 provides the six-membered counterpart and extends measured 2/1 983a604ac43bb4d41238. Together with m179, it tests whether ring expansion changes solvent sensitivity or mainly shifts the two endpoints together.

Previously unobserved meta-bromopropiophenone m64 at 50/1 is paired with its fluorinated analogue. Measured para-bromoacetophenone 605436d35600502e8c2e eluted substantially later than its acquisition prediction, motivating a test of transfer across substitution and side-chain environments.

m65 at 50/1 complements selected m64 at the same nominal sample volume and DCM plug, with density-derived amounts retained as covariates. Measured 5/1 c88ecd4aff975383199f anchors m65; the pair tests whether halogen-dependent differences increase in PE-rich mobile phase.

m30 at 10/1 fills the response curve below measured 50/1 605436d35600502e8c2e. It distinguishes a broad substitution-associated offset from a steep weak-solvent response and supports interpretation of the new m64/m65 comparison.

Previously unobserved dibromonaphthalene m5 at 20/1 tests structural transfer among fused, halogenated aromatics. Measured monobromonaphthalene 9a726343b54b1a50ebb9 provides related chemical coverage at a different ratio; this label tests the combined ring and halogen representation in a donor-free control.

Previously unobserved methyl alpha-bromoisobutyrate m93 at 20/1 closely matches the nominal loading protocol of ethyl analogue m76 in 41ae24734eabf9cae4d7. This ester-alkoxy comparison tests transfer in a compact-retention region and provides a control for the more strongly retained ester families.

Previously unobserved dimethyliodoarene m139 has only 0.429 maximum similarity to observed molecules, but a compact 5.34/11.44 mL prediction. Its label tests transfer to this substitution pattern and adds a zero-HBA heavy-halogen control alongside the polar response experiments.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-associated prediction failures are localized by structure and solvent ratio. Recent m90 strong-solvent labels were close, while m141 at 2/1 and 5/1 was overpredicted. Intermediate response curves and positional comparisons should therefore be more informative than a general upward nitrogen correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These comparisons can teach nitrogen environment, substitution, and ratio interactions while preventing a correction learned from severe historical failures from spreading to already accurate regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m211 transition between its measured 5/1 and 50/1 regimes, and do quinoline substitution and aminobenzonitrile position change the intermediate response?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic alcohol response depends on OH spacing, aromatic environment, additional acceptors, and loading conditions. The persistent m205 underestimate at 1/1 contrasts with the compact measured m206 1/1 response and the substantial completion volumes of m200.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Boundary and intermediate labels can separate environment-specific solvent response from a generic donor-count relationship and improve transfer among aromatic alcohols.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m205 become compact in pure EA, where does m206 lie at 2/1, and do nitro and bromo alcohols follow the response shapes predicted from existing alcohol coverage?

hypotheses.content: Loading may alter onset and completion differently depending on molecule and ratio. Some recorded differences may also reflect repeat variability. The predictor's near-invariance across selected loading pairs warrants controlled checks rather than assuming a universal loading direction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Fixed-protocol amount contrasts can reveal missing structure-by-loading and ratio-by-loading relationships. Existing same-tuple variation also limits how strongly individual differences should be generalized.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed plug conditions, do m72 at 10/1 and m81 at 50/1 show reproducible endpoint changes with sample amount, despite essentially invariant predictions?

hypotheses.content: PE-rich response curves may differ substantially across beta-dicarbonyl and ether-containing esters. The late m25 50/1 measurement warns against compressed extrapolation, while m81 and m107 observations show that neither completion growth nor loading behavior can be transferred uniformly across the family.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected curves test carbonyl arrangement, ester environment, and ether interactions across several related structures, allowing retraining to learn response slopes rather than isolated high-volume labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m26 and m13 exhibit the predicted steep growth, and does the simpler ether-acrylate m20 transfer the delayed behavior seen in m107?

hypotheses.content: Onset and completion need partly separate condition-response relationships. Unusual compact intervals or slight endpoint inconsistencies may reflect band-shape changes, loading effects, or recording variability; neighboring conditions are needed before treating them as stable response patterns.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels can constrain the joint V1/V2 mapping and distinguish onset shifts from completion changes without uniformly shifting both endpoints or imposing broad intervals everywhere.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: What is the actual m178 5/1 completion response, and does the m195 10/1-to-20/1 pair reproduce an abrupt change in onset or interval width?

hypotheses.content: Local substitution and fused-ring context may change aryl-ketone solvent sensitivity beyond a generic carbonyl relationship. Existing PE-rich ketone measurements differ substantially, but transfer to ring-expanded and meta-halogen analogues remains untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Ring-size and halogen comparisons offer interpretable tests of structural transfer across a well-represented functional group, connecting new molecules to observed response regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do ring expansion and meta Br/F substitution change the response slope, and does m30 already show delayed behavior at 10/1?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback reduced the value of treating historical nitrogen underestimation as a general acquisition argument. m90 at 0/1 and 1/1 and its 10/1 higher-loading row were close to their acquisition predictions, whereas m141 at 2/1 and 5/1 was overpredicted, especially for V2. The new nitrogen selections therefore emphasize missing transitions and matched structural comparisons. m205 at 1/1 remained substantially underestimated, supporting further investigation of its strong-solvent boundary; m119 at 2/1 was much closer, so another nearby m119 label has lower priority. The m25 50/1 result exposed a large failure on the PE-rich, weaker-mobile-phase side and motivates related carbonyl response curves. The m81 10/1 and 20/1 outcomes continued to show endpoint-specific loading behavior, while the m28 and m107 contrasts were more modest. Cinnamic acid at 10/1 again showed a substantial completion underestimate with accurate onset, preserving the endpoint-specific learning concern. Novel m190 and m200 acquisitions were close and m187/m214 completion predictions were moderately high, weakening any assumption that broad quantiles or novelty alone guarantee a large error. I also corrected the scientific memory against the observed table: 17ff70c0f8a083dcf5f0 is m126 at 10/1, not m178 at 5/1, so the latter remains an informative unmeasured condition. All historical errors are interpreted at acquisition time, not as current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure repair with response-curve experiments and interpretable structural exploration. Fixed-loading ratio pairs for m211, m26, m13, and m195 identify response shape; controlled amount pairs for m72 and m81 test loading relationships that the current predictions largely suppress. Alcohol selections examine environment-specific transfer after heterogeneous feedback. The cyclic-ketone and Br/F comparisons connect new structures to observed chemical families, while m5, m93, and m139 add controls in compact-retention regions. The m129 boundary point checks extrapolation after its intermediate curve has been measured. The selected experiments contain no duplicate molecule-plus-condition tuples. This allocation should help retraining learn relationships that recur across the Row-distribution, including separate onset and completion responses, without relying on extreme predicted volumes or quantile widths as acquisition objectives.
